krishna_summary: Bajaj Finserv is a major financial company running large lending and insurance businesses across India.
Company earnings and revenues have expanded steadily with solid contributions from its lending and insurance subsidiaries.
The stock price currently trades near ₹1998.0 but shows very low day-to-day trading participation.
Investors should watch whether customer loan demand and insurance growth stay resilient against market swings.
hanuman_section: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose ~19% YoY to ₹42,036.90 crore, with net profit rising ~18% to ₹6,296.67 crore.
Lending arm Bajaj Finance drove expansion with AUM up 24%, profit surging 28% YoY, and strong 19.1% ROE.
Valuations trade below historical benchmarks, with P/E at 31.2x-31.7x and P/B at 3.8x-4.1x below 5-year medians.
General insurance subsidiary demonstrated strong profitability, growing net profit 39% year-on-year to ₹576 crore.
vibhishana_section: Near-term price momentum is negative as MACD at 20.15 trails its signal line of 29.95.
Trading volume has collapsed to 0.05x of its 50-day average, showing severe lack of market participation.
Price trades below its 20-day SMA of ₹2025.50, reflecting short-term consolidation and softness.
Historical risk metrics show extreme annualized volatility of 190.38% and a past maximum drawdown of -86.55%.
yudhishthira_section: Filings present conflicting timeframes, citing Q1 FY25 profit of ₹2,138 crore alongside Q1 FY27 profit of ₹6,296.67 crore.
Conglomerate financial structure leaves key valuation metrics like EV/EBITDA completely unreported.
Quantitative strategy signals are split evenly at 11 bullish and 11 bearish, yielding a neutral 50 strategy score.
Extreme 1-year historical volatility of 190.38% contrasts sharply with recent stagnant trading volume.
vyasa_section: Core financial fundamentals remain sound, powered by double-digit profit growth across lending and insurance operations.
Valuation multiples remain discounted relative to the company's 5-year historical median levels.
Technical indicators show negative momentum and an acute volume drought below the 20-day moving average.
Reporting discrepancies between FY25 and FY27 filings require clarification before establishing higher conviction.
The current stance remains balanced until trading volume returns and price tests key structural boundaries.

Overhead resistance sits at ₹2119.30, with upper 52-week resistance marked at ₹2194.65.
The stock typically fluctuates by ₹29.31 in a standard trading session based on 14-day ATR.
Structural range boundaries reflect an upside breakout level at ₹2119.30 and a breakdown level at ₹1640.90.
watch: Price crossing above resistance at ₹2119.30 to indicate technical strength.
A decline below 50-day SMA support at ₹1926.43, which would invalidate the bullish trend bias.
Trading volume rising meaningfully from the current 0.05x 50-day average baseline.
Reconciliation and verification of reported Q1 FY25 versus Q1 FY27 financial results.

Trading well within its 52-week range of ₹1598.15 to ₹2194.65, situated between Bollinger bands of ₹1966.14 and ₹2084.86.
A 14-day ATR of ₹29.31 reflects daily price dispersion, while volume at 0.05x the 50-day average shows severe lack of participation.
Momentum is negative as MACD at 20.15 trails its signal line at 29.95, while RSI-14 remains neutral at 53.03.
The broader bullish bias would be invalidated if price breaks below the 50-day SMA support of ₹1926.43.
narada_section: Q1 FY25 consolidated total income rose 35% year-on-year to ₹31,480 crore.
Consolidated net profit grew 10% year-on-year to ₹2,138 crore in Q1 FY25.
General insurance subsidiary net profit expanded 39% year-on-year to ₹576 crore.
Stock trades at ₹1998.0 with strong trend strength and mixed strategy bias.
vidura_section: Consolidated total income rose ~19% YoY to ₹42,036.90 crore in Q1 FY27.
Consolidated profit after tax (PAT) grew ~18% YoY to ₹6,296.67 crore.
Lending arm Bajaj Finance drove overall growth with AUM rising 24% and PAT surging 28% YoY.
Lending subsidiary ROE stood strong at 19.1%, while life and general insurance segments showed steady expansion.
chanakya_section: Bajaj Finserv trades at a P/E of 31.2x-31.7x, below its 5-year historical median of 33.9x-35.2x (Value Research).
Current P/B multiple stands at 3.8x-4.1x, discounted relative to its 5-year median of 4.6x (Screener.in).
Financial sector peer group P/E averages approximately 33x across peers like Bajaj Holdings and Aditya Birla Capital (Simply Wall St).
EV/EBITDA is unknown due to conglomerate financial holding structure and standard reporting conventions.
Strong 1-year price performance of 573.54% and multi-line finance growth justify current multiples relative to historical averages.

glossary.P/E: Investors are paying this many rupees for every ₹1 the company earns in a year. High can mean expected growth, or an expensive price — it depends on the company.
glossary.P/B: The price compared to what the company's assets are worth on paper.
glossary.ROE: How much profit the company makes from the money shareholders put in. Higher is better.
glossary.ROCE: How well the company turns all its capital — including borrowed money — into profit.
glossary.EPS: The company's yearly profit divided across each share.
glossary.EV/EBITDA: The whole company's value compared to its operating earnings. Used to compare companies that carry different amounts of debt.
glossary.CAGR: The steady yearly rate that would have taken you from the starting value to today's.
glossary.RSI: A 0-100 momentum gauge. Above 70 means the price has run up fast; below 30 means it has fallen fast. Neither is a buy or sell signal on its own.
glossary.MACD: Compares a short-term and a long-term price average. Crossing above suggests momentum is turning up, below that it is turning down.
glossary.ATR: How much the price typically moves in a single day. A measure of choppiness.
glossary.AUM: The total money investors have put into this fund.
glossary.Expense Ratio: The yearly fee the fund charges, as a percentage of your money. It is already taken out of the NAV you see.
glossary.NAV: The per-unit price of the fund, updated at the end of each trading day.
glossary.Benchmark: The index the fund is trying to beat. Returns mean little without it.
glossary.Max Drawdown: The worst peak-to-bottom fall in the past. What a bad stretch has felt like.
glossary.Sharpe Ratio: Return earned per unit of bumpiness. Higher means a smoother ride for the same result.
glossary.Alpha: Return above what the benchmark delivered — the part credited to the manager.
glossary.Beta: How much the fund moves when the market moves. Above 1 swings harder than the market.
glossary.52-week range: The highest and lowest the price has been over the past year.
glossary.Exit Load: A fee charged if you sell your units before a set holding period.
